To: support@clockpoint.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: kevin.mutua@tausifreight.example
Subject: Re: [CP-48213] Overtime coding issue on night shifts

Dear Faith,

Here are the details you requested for ticket CP-48213:

1. Terminal model and firmware: The four BX-300 terminals at our Embakasi depot auto-updated from firmware 4.1.8 to 4.2.1 on the night of 27 October.

2. Shift template: NIGHT-8, scheduled from 22:00 to 06:00.

3. Example: Staff ID T-0417 clocked in at 21:54 on 30 October and clocked out at 06:07 on 31 October. All times are local Nairobi time.
   - Actual export: 2.1 hours REG on 30 October and 6.1 hours OT15 on 31 October.
   - Expected: 8.0 hours REG plus 0.2 hours OT15. Payroll rounds durations to the nearest tenth of an hour, so the total of 8 hours 13 minutes becomes 8.2 hours, with the 13 minutes outside the scheduled shift coded OT15.

4. Export profile: Payroll CSV v2.

5. First noticed: Kevin identified the problem on 5 November while reviewing draft October overtime. The affected exports date from about 28 October, immediately after the update.

Shifts crossing midnight are being split into two lines, with the after-midnight portion incorrectly coded OT15 instead of REG. This affects 38 night-shift staff and overstated draft October overtime by approximately KES 212,000. Kevin has held the overtime lines and corrected them manually from raw punches, but this is not sustainable. Mombasa Road day shifts are unaffected; its two terminals remain on 4.1.8.

Your release notes promised improved midnight rollover handling, but we are seeing the opposite following this update.

Please provide a fix or clear workaround before our payroll cut-off on 20 November. I have copied Kevin Mutua, our payroll officer, who will test your proposed solution.

Can Brian Ochieng, our IT colleague who manages the terminals, safely roll the Embakasi terminals back to 4.1.8 without losing punch data? Please confirm any backup steps or precautions before he proceeds.

Regards,
Njeri Mwangi
HR Manager
Tausi Freight
